title: Real Wages Are Falling Going Into the Midterms
summary: Chart segment comparing real wages in Trump's second term and Bush's: Trump led early but real wages flatlined, while Bush's rose as gas prices moderated.

assertions.quote: under Trump, they actually came down and a flatlined. So, again, voters are looking at no real wage increases under Trump.
Trump actually was performing better on wages for the first year and a half of this term.
even when wages are going up, the people at the bottom are being left behind and it's much worse for them

verdicts.note: In 2021-24 low-wage workers saw the fastest real gains; in 2026 production workers' real pay fell slightly more than the average.

assertions.quote: when gas prices start and other prices moderated under Bush, his real wages, people actually their purchasing power actually went up

verdicts.note: Gasoline is a large, fast-moving CPI component, so a fuel drop lowers headline inflation within a month and raises real pay.

In June 2026 the seasonally adjusted gasoline index fell 9.7%, pulling all-items CPI down 0.4% while nominal AHE rose 0.3%, and derived real hourly earnings jumped 0.7% in the month (11.225 to 11.303), reversing most of the spring's loss; one episode, but it shows the mechanism.
